source_refs.note: Book p. 248-254: 13.6 Theorems on Differentiation; rules 1-2, run-in rules 3-6 (constant multiple, sum/difference, product, quotient) with proofs, Note box, Examples 6-11

blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum bachon! Pichle sabaq mein hum ne derivative ko definition (first principle) se nikalna seekha tha: Step I se Step IV tak, \(\delta x\) aur \(\delta y\) bana kar, phir limit le kar. Yeh tareeqa bunyaadi hai, lekin har sawal mein itna lamba kaam karna thaka deta hai. Aaj hum chand aise rules (qawaid) seekhenge jo ek baar definition se saabit ho jaate hain, aur phir hum unhein seedha istemal karte hain. Socho jaise multiplication table: ek baar samajh li, phir har baar dobara jama kar ke nahin nikalte.
Ab tak hum do formulas saabit kar chuke hain (kitab yahan \"tow formula\" chhaapti hai, jo asal mein \"two formulas\" hai):

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab "the following tow formula" chhaapti hai. Sahi lafz "the following two formulas" (do formulas) hai. Yeh sirf spelling ki ghalti hai, maths par koi asar nahin.

items: \(\frac{d}{dx}(c) = 0\), yani constant function (jo badalta hi nahin) ka derivative zero hota hai.
\(\frac{d}{dx}(x^{n}) = nx^{n-1}\): yeh power formula (power rule) hai, jab \(n\) koi bhi real number ho.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Pehla rule zero kyun deta hai? \(y = c\) ka graph ek seedhi ufuqi (horizontal) line hai. Is ki oonchai kabhi nahin badalti, is liye \(\delta y = c - c = 0\) hai, chahe \(\delta x\) kitna bhi ho. Jab tabdeeli hi zero hai to rate of change (slope) bhi zero. Misal: agar aap ki jeb mein hamesha 50 rupay hi rehte hain, to har ghante un ki tabdeeli ka rate zero hai.
Power rule ko yaad karne ka aasan tareeqa: \"power ko neeche utaar kar aage multiply karo, phir power mein se 1 ghata do\". Kitab ne 13.4 mein ise integer \(n\) ke liye saabit kiya tha aur rational \(n\) ke liye bataya tha. Yeh har real \(n\) ke liye sahi hai (\(x > 0\) par); irrational power ka proof aage ki classes mein aata hai.
Khud sochiye: \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^{5}) = ?\), \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^{-1}) = ?\), \(\frac{d}{dx}(\sqrt{x}) = ?\)
Jawab: \(5x^{4}\); \(-x^{-2} = -\frac{1}{x^{2}}\); aur \(\sqrt{x} = x^{1/2}\), is liye \(\frac{1}{2}x^{-1/2} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\).

Ab hum kuch aur zaroori formulas (rules) saabit karenge jin se mukhtalif functions ke derivatives jaldi aur aasani se nikal jaate hain. Aage ki saari guftagu mein \(f\), \(g\), \(h\) wagaira aise functions hain jo \(x\) par differentiable hain (yani un ka derivative \(x\) par maujood hai), jab tak kuch aur na kaha jaye.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab in rules ko number deti hai: 1, 2 (upar wale), phir 3, 4, 5, 6. Examples mein likha hota hai \"Using formula 3\" ya \"Using formulas 3 and 4\". Is liye numbers yaad rakhiye, warna examples parhte waqt pata nahin chalega ke kaun sa rule laga. Har rule ka proof wahi chaar qadam wala tareeqa hai jo aap 13.3.2 mein seekh chuke hain: \(x + \delta x\) par value, tabdeeli, \(\delta x\) se taqseem, aur limit.
3. Derivative of \(y = cf(x)\)

Pehle samajhte hain ke yeh rule kehta kya hai: agar kisi function ke saath ek constant multiply ho raha ho (jaise \(5x^{2}\) mein 5), to derivative lete waqt woh constant bahar hi khara rehta hai. Ab isay saabit karte hain, qadam ba qadam.

Proof: Maan lijiye \(y = cf(x)\). To
(i) \(x\) ko \(\delta x\) barhayein to \(y\) bhi \(\delta y\) barhega: \(y + \delta y = cf(x + \delta x)\)
(ii) Is mein se asal \(y\) ghata dein: \(y + \delta y - y = cf(x + \delta x) - cf(x)\)
yani \(\delta y = c[f(x + \delta x) - f(x)]\) (\(c\) common nikaal liya)
(iii) Dono taraf \(\delta x\) se divide karein:
\[\dfrac{\delta y}{\delta x} = c\left[\dfrac{f(x+\delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\right]\]
Ab \(\delta x \to 0\) par limit lein:
(iv)
\[\lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{\delta y}{\delta x} = \lim_{\delta x \to 0}\, c\cdot\dfrac{f(x+\delta x)-f(x)}{\delta x}\]
\[= c\lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{f(x+\delta x)-f(x)}{\delta x}\]
Constant factor ko limit ke nishaan se bahar nikala ja sakta hai, kyun ke \(\delta x\) badalne se \(c\) par koi asar nahin parta.
Is tarah \(\frac{dy}{dx} = cf'(x)\), yani \([cf(x)]' = cf'(x)\), ya

blocks.text_alt: d by d x of c times f of x equals c times d by d x of f of x

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Iska matlab tasveer mein dekhiye: agar graph ki har oonchai \(c\) guna kar di jaye (graph ko upar ki taraf khench diya jaye), to har chadhai \(\delta y\) bhi \(c\) guna ho jati hai, aur slope bhi \(c\) guna. Is liye constant bahar aa jata hai.
Hamari taraf se misaal: \(\frac{d}{dx}(7x^{3}) = 7\cdot\frac{d}{dx}(x^{3}) = 7\cdot 3x^{2} = 21x^{2}\).
Dhyan dein: yeh rule sirf multiply hone wale constant ke liye hai. Jama hone wala constant (jaise \(x^{3} + 7\) mein 7) bahar nahin rehta, us ka derivative zero ho jata hai (formula 1).
Ab kitab ki misaal dekhte hain jis mein formula 3 aur power rule dono saath lagte hain.

blocks.title: Example 6
steps:
Given: \(y = 3x^{\frac{4}{3}}\).
To find: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Method: sab se pehle function ki shakal pehchaaniye: ek constant (3) aur us ke saath \(x\) ki power (\(\frac{4}{3}\)). Constant ke liye formula 3, aur power ke liye power rule. Power fraction mein hai, lekin power rule har real power ke liye chalta hai, is liye ghabraane ki zaroorat nahin.

Step 1: Constant ko bahar nikaalein (Formula 3)
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(3x^{\frac{4}{3}}\right) = 3\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^{\frac{4}{3}}\right)\]
Kyun: formula 3 mein \(c = 3\) aur \(f(x) = x^{\frac{4}{3}}\) hai. Constant ko bahar rakhne se kaam saaf rehta hai: ab sirf \(x^{\frac{4}{3}}\) ka derivative chahiye.

Step 2: Power rule lagayein
\[= 3 \times \dfrac{4}{3}x^{\frac{4}{3}-1}\]
\[= 3 \times \dfrac{4}{3}x^{\frac{1}{3}}\]
Kyun: power \(n = \frac{4}{3}\) neeche aa kar multiply hoti hai, aur nayi power \(\frac{4}{3} - 1\) hai. Fraction mein se 1 ghatane ke liye 1 ko \(\frac{3}{3}\) likhiye: \(\frac{4}{3} - \frac{3}{3} = \frac{1}{3}\).
Dhyan dein: bohat se bachay \(\frac{4}{3} - 1\) ko \(\frac{3}{3}\) ya \(\frac{4}{2}\) likh dete hain. Numerator mein se hi denominator jitna ghataiye.

Step 3: Hal kar ke saaf likhein
\[= 4x^{\frac{1}{3}}\]
Kyun: \(3 \times \frac{4}{3} = 4\); 3 aur 3 cancel ho gaye. Kitab ke saath milaiye: wahan bhi yahi \(4x^{\frac{1}{3}}\) hai.

Tasdeeq:
Ab dekhte hain jawab sahi hai ya nahin. \(x = 8\) lein: hamara jawab \(4 \cdot 8^{1/3} = 4 \cdot 2 = 8\) deta hai.
Definition wala chhota hisaab: \(\frac{3(8.001)^{4/3} - 3(8)^{4/3}}{0.001} \approx 8.0002\). Yeh 8 ke bilkul qareeb hai, is liye jawab durust hai.

blocks.text: 4. Derivative of a sum or a difference of functions

Yeh rule shayad sab se zyada kaam aane wala hai. Is ka seedha matlab: agar do functions jama (ya tafreeq) ho rahe hon, to un ke derivatives bhi alag alag nikaal kar jama (ya tafreeq) kar do. Agar \(f\) aur \(g\) \(x\) par differentiable hain, to \(f + g\) aur \(f - g\) bhi differentiable hain, aur

blocks.text_alt: the derivative of f of x plus g of x equals f prime of x plus g prime of x

blocks.text: yani \(\frac{d}{dx}[f(x)+g(x)] = \frac{d}{dx}[f(x)] + \frac{d}{dx}[g(x)]\).

blocks.text_alt: the derivative of f of x minus g of x equals f prime of x minus g prime of x

blocks.text: Aur isi tarah \(\frac{d}{dx}[f(x)-g(x)] = \frac{d}{dx}[f(x)] - \frac{d}{dx}[g(x)]\).

Proof: Maan lijiye \(\phi(x) = f(x) + g(x)\) (\(\phi\) ko \"phi\" parhte hain; yeh sirf naye function ka naam hai). To
(i) \(\phi(x + \delta x) = f(x + \delta x) + g(x + \delta x)\)
(ii) Tabdeeli nikaalein:
\[\phi(x+\delta x) - \phi(x)\]
\[= f(x+\delta x) + g(x+\delta x) - [f(x) + g(x)]\]
\[= [f(x+\delta x) - f(x)] + [g(x+\delta x) - g(x)]\]
(terms ki tarteeb badal kar \(f\) wale saath aur \(g\) wale saath rakh diye)
(iii) \(\delta x\) se divide karein:
\[\dfrac{\phi(x+\delta x)-\phi(x)}{\delta x} = \dfrac{f(x+\delta x)-f(x)}{\delta x} + \dfrac{g(x+\delta x)-g(x)}{\delta x}\]
\(\delta x \to 0\) par limit lein:
(iv)
\[\lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{\phi(x+\delta x)-\phi(x)}{\delta x}\]
\[= \lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{f(x+\delta x)-f(x)}{\delta x} + \lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{g(x+\delta x)-g(x)}{\delta x}\]
(Jama ki limit, limits ka jama hoti hai: yeh Unit 12 ka limit theorem hai)
\[\phi'(x) = f'(x) + g'(x)\]
yani \([f(x) + g(x)]' = f'(x) + g'(x)\), ya \(\frac{d}{dx}[f(x)+g(x)] = \frac{d}{dx}[f(x)] + \frac{d}{dx}[g(x)]\).
Doosre hisse (minus wale) ka proof bilkul isi tarah hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kitab minus wala proof chhor deti hai, to hum mukhtasar dekh lete hain: \(\phi(x) = f(x) - g(x)\) lein. To \(\phi(x+\delta x) - \phi(x) = [f(x+\delta x) - f(x)] - [g(x+\delta x) - g(x)]\). \(\delta x\) se divide kar ke limit lein (tafreeq ki limit, limits ki tafreeq hai), to \(\phi'(x) = f'(x) - g'(x)\).
Amli matlab: lambi expression ko term by term (ek ek term kar ke) differentiate karo, aur har term ka plus ya minus sign waisa hi rehne do.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Sum ya difference wala formula do se zyada functions par bhi lagaya ja sakta hai (jaise 5 terms ho to 5 alag derivatives jama karein).

Ab teen examples aate hain. Example 7 mein paanch terms ka jama hai; Example 8 aur 9 mein pehle bracket khol kar ya simplify kar ke expression ko powers ke jama mein badla jata hai, phir yahi rules lagte hain.

blocks.title: Example 7
steps:
Given: \(y = \frac{3}{4}x^{4} + \frac{2}{3}x^{3} + \frac{1}{2}x^{2} + 2x + 5\).
To find: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Method: sab se pehle dekhte hain ke \(y\) kaisa hai: paanch terms ka jama. Formula 4 (Note ke mutabiq do se zyada terms par bhi) kehta hai ke har term ka alag derivative lo. Har term mein ek constant multiply ho raha hai, us ke liye formula 3; akela constant 5 ke liye formula 1; aur powers ke liye power rule.

Step 1: Terms ko alag karein (Formula 4)
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{3}{4}x^{4}\right) + \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{2}{3}x^{3}\right)\]
\[+ \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}x^{2}\right) + \dfrac{d}{dx}(2x) + \dfrac{d}{dx}(5)\]
Kyun: jama ka derivative, derivatives ka jama hai. Ab ek bara sawal paanch chhote aasan sawalon mein toot gaya.

Step 2: Constants bahar (Formulas 3 aur 1)
\[= \dfrac{3}{4}\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{4}) + \dfrac{2}{3}\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{3})\]
\[+ \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{2}) + 2\dfrac{d}{dx}(x) + 0\]
Kyun: multiply hone wale constants (\(\frac{3}{4}, \frac{2}{3}, \frac{1}{2}, 2\)) formula 3 se bahar aa gaye. Akela 5 constant function hai, us ka derivative formula 1 se zero.

Step 3: Power formula
\[= \dfrac{3}{4}(4x^{4-1}) + \dfrac{2}{3}(3x^{3-1})\]
\[+ \dfrac{1}{2}(2x^{2-1}) + 2(1\cdot x^{1-1})\]
Kyun: har power \(n\) neeche aayi aur power ek kam hui. Aakhri term mein \(x = x^{1}\), is ka derivative \(1\cdot x^{0} = 1\) hai (kyun ke \(x^{0} = 1\)).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{d}{dx}(x) = 1\) hai, \(x\) ya 0 nahin. Yeh bohat aam ghalti hai.

Step 4: Simplify karein
\[= 3x^{3} + 2x^{2} + x + 2\]
Kyun: \(\frac{3}{4}\cdot 4 = 3\), \(\frac{2}{3}\cdot 3 = 2\), \(\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2 = 1\), \(2\cdot 1 = 2\). Dekhiye kitab ne fractions aise chune ke har coefficient poora number ban jaye.

Tasdeeq:
Ek chhota shortcut: \(\frac{d}{dx}(ax^{n}) = anx^{n-1}\). Har term par lagaiye: \(\frac{3}{4}x^{4} \to 3x^{3}\), \(\frac{2}{3}x^{3} \to 2x^{2}\), \(\frac{1}{2}x^{2} \to x\), \(2x \to 2\), \(5 \to 0\). Wahi jawab aaya, is liye hamara kaam durust hai.

blocks.title: Example 8
blocks.problem: Find the derivative of \(y = (x^{2} - 5)(x^{3} + 7)\) with respect to \(x\).
steps:
Given: \(y = (x^{2} - 5)(x^{3} + 7)\).
To find: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Method: abhi tak humare paas product (zarb) ka rule nahin aaya (woh formula 5 hai, aage aa raha hai). Is liye pehle brackets khol kar \(y\) ko powers ka jama bana lete hain; phir formulas 3 aur 4 aur power rule kaafi hain.

Step 1: Brackets kholein
\[y = (x^{2} - 5)(x^{3} + 7)\]
\[= x^{5} + 7x^{2} - 5x^{3} - 35\]
\[= x^{5} - 5x^{3} + 7x^{2} - 35\]
Kyun: pehle bracket ki har term doosre bracket ki har term se multiply hoti hai: \(x^{2}\cdot x^{3} = x^{5}\) (powers jama hoti hain), \(x^{2}\cdot 7 = 7x^{2}\), \((-5)\cdot x^{3} = -5x^{3}\), \((-5)\cdot 7 = -35\). Phir powers ki tarteeb se likh diya.
Dhyan dein: kitab ka sawal \(x^{2} - 5\) hai, lekin kitab ke hal mein \(x^{2} + 5\) le kar bracket khola gaya hai. Hum chhapa hua sawal hi hal kar rahe hain (neeche \"Kitab ki ghalti\" dekhiye).

Step 2: Term by term differentiate karein (Formulas 3 aur 4)
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{5}) - 5\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{3})\]
\[+ 7\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^{2}) - \dfrac{d}{dx}(35)\]
Kyun: formula 4 jama aur tafreeq ko alag karta hai, formula 3 constants 5 aur 7 ko bahar nikaalta hai. Minus sign apni jagah qaim rehta hai.

Step 3: Power formula
\[= 5x^{5-1} - 5 \times 3x^{3-1} + 7 \times 2x^{2-1} - 0\]
\[= 5x^{4} - 15x^{2} + 14x\]
Kyun: har power par power rule; constant 35 ka derivative zero. \(5 \times 3 = 15\) aur \(7 \times 2 = 14\).

Tasdeeq:
Aage aane wala product rule (formula 5) laga kar dekhte hain: \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^{2} - 5) = 2x\) aur \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^{3} + 7) = 3x^{2}\). To
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x(x^{3} + 7) + (x^{2} - 5)(3x^{2})\]
\[= 2x^{4} + 14x + 3x^{4} - 15x^{2}\]
\[= 5x^{4} - 15x^{2} + 14x\]
Do alag tareeqon se ek hi jawab: bilkul pakka.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Sawal mein \(y = (x^{2} - 5)(x^{3} + 7)\) chhapa hai, lekin kitab ke hal mein \((x^{2} + 5)(x^{3} + 7) = x^{5} + 5x^{3} + 7x^{2} + 35\) khola gaya aur jawab \(5x^{4} + 15x^{2} + 14x\) aaya. Chhape hue sawal ke liye bracket \(x^{5} - 5x^{3} + 7x^{2} - 35\) banta hai aur sahi derivative \(5x^{4} - 15x^{2} + 14x\) hai. (Kitab ka kaam \(+5\) wale sawal ke liye theek hai.)

blocks.title: Example 9
steps:
Given: \(y = (2\sqrt{x} + 2)(x - \sqrt{x})\), jahan \(x > 0\).
To find: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Method: yahan bhi product hai, lekin kitab ek khoobsurat shortcut dikhati hai: pehle factorise (common nikaal kar) kar ke \(y\) ko sirf do powers ki tafreeq bana do. Phir formulas 3, 4 aur power rule se derivative foran nikal aata hai.

Step 1: Har bracket se common nikaalein
\[y = 2(\sqrt{x} + 1)\cdot\sqrt{x}(\sqrt{x} - 1)\]
\[= 2\sqrt{x}(\sqrt{x} + 1)(\sqrt{x} - 1)\]
Kyun: pehle bracket mein 2 common hai: \(2\sqrt{x} + 2 = 2(\sqrt{x} + 1)\). Doosre mein \(x = \sqrt{x}\cdot\sqrt{x}\), is liye \(x - \sqrt{x} = \sqrt{x}\cdot\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{x}\cdot 1 = \sqrt{x}(\sqrt{x} - 1)\). Yeh \(x = (\sqrt{x})^{2}\) wala nukta yaad rakhiye, bohat kaam aata hai.

Step 2: Difference of squares, phir powers
\[y = 2\sqrt{x}(x - 1)\]
\[= 2\left(x^{\frac{3}{2}} - x^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)\]
Kyun: \((a + b)(a - b) = a^{2} - b^{2}\) wala formula: \((\sqrt{x} + 1)(\sqrt{x} - 1) = (\sqrt{x})^{2} - 1 = x - 1\). Phir \(\sqrt{x}\cdot x = x^{\frac{1}{2}}\cdot x^{1} = x^{\frac{1}{2}+1} = x^{\frac{3}{2}}\) (same base ki powers multiply hon to jama hoti hain).

Step 3: Differentiate karein (Formulas 3 aur 4)
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2\left[\dfrac{d}{dx}x^{\frac{3}{2}} - \dfrac{d}{dx}x^{\frac{1}{2}}\right]\]
Kyun: constant 2 bahar (formula 3), aur tafreeq ka derivative term by term (formula 4).

Step 4: Power rule
\[= 2\left[\dfrac{3}{2}x^{\frac{3}{2}-1} - \dfrac{1}{2}x^{\frac{1}{2}-1}\right]\]
\[= 3x^{\frac{1}{2}} - x^{-\frac{1}{2}}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{3}{2} - 1 = \frac{1}{2}\) aur \(\frac{1}{2} - 1 = -\frac{1}{2}\). Bahar wala 2 andar multiply hua: \(2\cdot\frac{3}{2} = 3\), \(2\cdot\frac{1}{2} = 1\).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{1}{2} - 1\) negative hai, \(-\frac{1}{2}\). Is minus ko bhoolna aam ghalti hai.

Step 5: Roots mein likh kar ek denominator banayein
\[= 3\sqrt{x} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\]
\[= \dfrac{3x - 1}{\sqrt{x}}\]
Kyun: negative power ka matlab ulta (reciprocal): \(x^{-\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\). Common denominator \(\sqrt{x}\) banane ke liye \(3\sqrt{x}\) ko \(\frac{3\sqrt{x}\cdot\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x}} = \frac{3x}{\sqrt{x}}\) likha.

Tasdeeq:
\(x = 4\) par: hamara jawab \(\frac{12 - 1}{2} = 5.5\). Function se seedha hisaab: \(\frac{y(4.001) - y(3.999)}{0.002} \approx 5.5000\). Aur agla Example 10 isi function ko product rule se hal kar ke bhi yahi jawab deta hai.

blocks.text: 5. Derivative of a Product (The Product Rule)

Ab woh rule jis ka intezaar tha: do functions ka product (zarb). Yahan sab se badi ghalti yeh hoti hai ke bachay sochte hain \"product ka derivative = derivatives ka product\". Yeh bilkul ghalat hai, aur abhi hum dekhenge ke sahi formula kya hai aur kyun. Agar \(f\) aur \(g\) \(x\) par differentiable hain, to \(fg\) bhi differentiable hai aur \([f(x)g(x)]' = f'(x)g(x) + f(x)g'(x)\), yani

blocks.text_alt: d by d x of f of x times g of x equals the derivative of f times g of x plus f of x times the derivative of g

blocks.text:
Proof: Maan lijiye \(\phi(x) = f(x)g(x)\). To
(i) \(\phi(x + \delta x) = f(x + \delta x)\,g(x + \delta x)\)
(ii) \(\phi(x + \delta x) - \phi(x) = f(x + \delta x)\,g(x + \delta x) - f(x)\,g(x)\)
Ab ek chalaak qadam: step (ii) mein \(f(x)\,g(x + \delta x)\) ko ek dafa ghatayein aur ek dafa jama karein (is se value nahin badalti):
\[\phi(x+\delta x) - \phi(x)\]
\[= f(x+\delta x)g(x+\delta x) - f(x)g(x+\delta x)\]
\[\quad + f(x)g(x+\delta x) - f(x)g(x)\]
\[= [f(x+\delta x) - f(x)]\,g(x+\delta x)\]
\[\quad + f(x)[g(x+\delta x) - g(x)]\]
(iii) \(\delta x\) se divide karein:
\[\dfrac{\phi(x+\delta x)-\phi(x)}{\delta x} = \left[\dfrac{f(x+\delta x)-f(x)}{\delta x}\right]g(x+\delta x) + f(x)\left[\dfrac{g(x+\delta x)-g(x)}{\delta x}\right]\]
\(\delta x \to 0\) par limit lein:
(iv)
\[\lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{\phi(x+\delta x)-\phi(x)}{\delta x}\]
\[= \lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{f(x+\delta x)-f(x)}{\delta x}\cdot\lim_{\delta x \to 0}g(x+\delta x)\]
\[\quad + \lim_{\delta x \to 0}f(x)\cdot\lim_{\delta x \to 0}\dfrac{g(x+\delta x)-g(x)}{\delta x}\]
(limit theorems se: jama ki limit = limits ka jama, product ki limit = limits ka product)
Is tarah \(\phi'(x) = f'(x)\,g(x) + f(x)\,g'(x)\), kyun ke \(\lim_{\delta x \to 0} g(x + \delta x) = g(x)\),
ya \(\frac{d}{dx}[f(x)\cdot g(x)] = \frac{d}{dx}[f(x)]\cdot g(x) + f(x)\left[\frac{d}{dx}g(x)\right]\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is proof mein do khaas baatein hain:
1. \"Ghatao aur jama karo\" wali chaal: \(f(x)g(x + \delta x)\) ko ghata kar wapas jama karne se value wahi rehti hai, lekin expression do hisson mein bat jata hai: ek mein sirf \(f\) ki tabdeeli, doosre mein sirf \(g\) ki. Yeh trick math mein bohat jagah kaam aati hai.
2. \(\lim_{\delta x \to 0} g(x + \delta x) = g(x)\) kyun? Kyun ke \(g\) differentiable hai, aur 13.5 mein hum ne parha ke har differentiable function continuous hota hai. Continuous ka matlab hi yeh hai ke \(x\) ke qareeb jaane par value \(g(x)\) ke qareeb jati hai.
Yaad karne ka jumla: \"pehle ka derivative guna doosra, jama pehla guna doosre ka derivative\".
Hamari taraf se misaal: \(\frac{d}{dx}[x^{2}(x + 1)] = 2x(x + 1) + x^{2}(1) = 3x^{2} + 2x\). Bracket khol kar dekhein: \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^{3} + x^{2}) = 3x^{2} + 2x\). Dono barabar!
Khud sochiye: \(\frac{d}{dx}(x \cdot x)\) ka jawab kya hai? Agar koi \(1 \cdot 1 = 1\) kahe to woh ghalat hai; product rule se \(1\cdot x + x\cdot 1 = 2x\), jo \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^{2}) = 2x\) se milta hai.
Ab Example 9 wala hi function dobara lete hain, lekin is dafa product rule se. Is se aap ko dono tareeqon ka farq bhi samajh aa jayega.

blocks.title: Example 10
blocks.problem: Find derivative of \(y = (2\sqrt{x} + 2)(x - \sqrt{x})\) with respect to \(x\).
steps:
Given: \(y = (2\sqrt{x} + 2)(x - \sqrt{x})\), \(x > 0\).
To find: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) (wahi function jo Example 9 mein tha, ab product rule se).
Method: \(y\) do functions ka product hai, is liye formula 5 bilkul fit hai. Kaam halka karne ke liye pehle bracket se 2 common nikaal lete hain (formula 3).

Step 1: Constant bahar nikaalein
\[y = 2(\sqrt{x} + 1)(x - \sqrt{x})\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[(\sqrt{x} + 1)(x - \sqrt{x})\right]\]
Kyun: \(2\sqrt{x} + 2 = 2(\sqrt{x} + 1)\), aur formula 3 ke mutabiq constant 2 derivative ke bahar rehta hai. Chhote numbers ke saath ghalti ka imkaan kam hota hai.

Step 2: Product rule lagayein
\[= 2\Big[\Big(\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sqrt{x} + 1)\Big)(x - \sqrt{x})\]
\[\quad + (\sqrt{x} + 1)\dfrac{d}{dx}(x - \sqrt{x})\Big]\]
Kyun: formula 5 mein \(f(x) = \sqrt{x} + 1\) (pehla) aur \(g(x) = x - \sqrt{x}\) (doosra). \"Pehle ka derivative guna doosra, jama pehla guna doosre ka derivative.\"

Step 3: Dono hisson ke derivatives
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sqrt{x} + 1) = \dfrac{1}{2}x^{\frac{1}{2}-1} + 0 = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\]
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(x - \sqrt{x}) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}x^{\frac{1}{2}-1} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{x} = x^{\frac{1}{2}}\), power rule se \(\frac{1}{2}x^{-\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\). Constant 1 ka derivative 0, aur \(x\) ka derivative 1. Yeh \(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\) wala natija zabani yaad kar lein; har jagah kaam aata hai.

Step 4: Values rakhein aur doosre bracket ko ek fraction banayein
\[= 2\Big[\dfrac{x - \sqrt{x}}{2\sqrt{x}} + (\sqrt{x} + 1)\Big(\dfrac{2\sqrt{x} - 1}{2\sqrt{x}}\Big)\Big]\]
Kyun: \(1 - \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} = \frac{2\sqrt{x}}{2\sqrt{x}} - \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} = \frac{2\sqrt{x} - 1}{2\sqrt{x}}\). Ab dono terms ka denominator ek jaisa (\(2\sqrt{x}\)) ho gaya.
Dhyan dein: kitab is line mein \(\sqrt{x} + 1\) se pehle khulne wala bracket \"(\" chhapna bhool gayi hai; hum ne sahi likha hai.

Step 5: Common denominator bahar nikaalein
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\left[x - \sqrt{x} + (\sqrt{x} + 1)(2\sqrt{x} - 1)\right]\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\left[x - \sqrt{x} + 2x - \sqrt{x} + 2\sqrt{x} - 1\right]\]
Kyun: bahar wala 2 aur denominator ka 2 cancel: \(2 \times \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\). Phir \((\sqrt{x} + 1)(2\sqrt{x} - 1)\) khola: \(\sqrt{x}\cdot 2\sqrt{x} = 2x\), \(\sqrt{x}\cdot(-1) = -\sqrt{x}\), \(1\cdot 2\sqrt{x} = 2\sqrt{x}\), \(1\cdot(-1) = -1\).

Step 6: Milti julti terms jama karein
\[= \dfrac{3x - 1}{\sqrt{x}}\]
Kyun: \(x + 2x = 3x\), aur \(-\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{x} + 2\sqrt{x} = 0\): saari root wali terms khatam ho gayin.

Tasdeeq:
Example 9 mein isi function ko pehle simplify kar ke bhi \(\frac{3x - 1}{\sqrt{x}}\) mila tha. Do mukhtalif raaste, ek manzil: jawab pakka hai. Sabaq: jab expression aasani se simplify ho jaye (Example 9) to woh raasta chhota hai; warna product rule hamesha kaam karta hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Hal ki paanchvi line mein kitab \(\sqrt{x}+1\) se pehle khulne wala bracket chhapna bhool gayi hai. Sahi line: \(2\left[\frac{x-\sqrt{x}}{2\sqrt{x}} + (\sqrt{x}+1)\left(\frac{2\sqrt{x}-1}{2\sqrt{x}}\right)\right]\). Aakhri jawab \(\frac{3x - 1}{\sqrt{x}}\) sahi hai.
6. Derivative of a Quotient (The Quotient Rule)

Aakhri rule: do functions ki taqseem (quotient), yani fraction. Agar \(f\) aur \(g\) \(x\) par differentiable hon aur \(D(g)\) ke kisi bhi \(x\) ke liye \(g(x) \ne 0\) ho (kyun ke zero se divide nahin kar sakte), to \(\frac{f}{g}\) bhi \(x\) par differentiable hai aur

blocks.text_alt: the derivative of f of x over g of x equals f prime of x times g of x minus f of x times g prime of x, all over g of x squared

blocks.text: yani \(\frac{d}{dx}\left[\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}\right] = \frac{\left[\frac{d}{dx}f(x)\right]g(x) - f(x)\left[\frac{d}{dx}g(x)\right]}{[g(x)]^{2}}\).

Proof: Maan lijiye \(\phi(x) = \frac{f(x)}{g(x)}\). To
(i) \(\phi(x + \delta x) = \frac{f(x + \delta x)}{g(x + \delta x)}\)
(ii) Tabdeeli; do fractions ko ek common denominator par laayein:
\[\phi(x+\delta x) - \phi(x) = \dfrac{f(x+\delta x)}{g(x+\delta x)} - \dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}\]
\[= \dfrac{f(x+\delta x)g(x) - f(x)g(x+\delta x)}{g(x)\,g(x+\delta x)}\]
Product rule jaisi chaal: numerator mein \(f(x)g(x)\) ko ghatayein aur jama karein:
\[\phi(x+\delta x) - \phi(x)\]
\[= \dfrac{f(x+\delta x)g(x) - f(x)g(x) - f(x)g(x+\delta x) + f(x)g(x)}{g(x)\,g(x+\delta x)}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{g(x)\,g(x+\delta x)}\Big[\big(f(x+\delta x) - f(x)\big)g(x) - f(x)\big(g(x+\delta x) - g(x)\big)\Big]\]
(iii) \(\delta x\) se divide karein:
\[\dfrac{\phi(x+\delta x)-\phi(x)}{\delta x}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{g(x)\,g(x+\delta x)}\Big[\dfrac{f(x+\delta x)-f(x)}{\delta x}\cdot g(x) - f(x)\cdot\dfrac{g(x+\delta x)-g(x)}{\delta x}\Big]\]
(iv) \(\delta x \to 0\) par limit lein. Limit theorems aur \(\lim_{\delta x \to 0} g(x + \delta x) = g(x)\) se:
\[\phi'(x) = \dfrac{1}{g(x)\cdot g(x)}[f'(x)g(x) - f(x)g'(x)]\]
Is tarah

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Proof ke steps (iii) aur (iv) mein kitab aakhri fraction ko \(\frac{g(x+\delta x-g(x)}{\delta x}\) chhaapti hai, yani bracket ghalat jagah band hua hai. Sahi \(\frac{g(x+\delta x)-g(x)}{\delta x}\) hai: yeh \(g\) ka difference quotient hai jis ki limit \(g'(x)\) hai. Hum ne upar sahi shakal likhi hai.

blocks.text_alt: the derivative of f over g equals f prime g minus f g prime, over g squared

blocks.text: ya \(\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}\right) = \frac{\left[\frac{d}{dx}(f(x))\right]g(x) - f(x)\left[\frac{d}{dx}(g(x))\right]}{[g(x)]^{2}}\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yaad karne ka jumla: \"neeche wala guna upar wale ka derivative, minus upar wala guna neeche wale ka derivative, sab ko neeche wale ke square se divide\".
Product rule mein tarteeb se farq nahin parta tha (jama hai), lekin yahan minus hai, is liye TARTEEB bohat zaroori hai: pehle \(f'g\), phir \(-fg'\). Ulta likhenge to jawab ka sign ulat jayega.
Hamari taraf se misaal: \(\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)\). Yahan \(f = 1\), \(g = x\), \(f' = 0\), \(g' = 1\): \(\frac{0\cdot x - 1\cdot 1}{x^{2}} = -\frac{1}{x^{2}}\). Power rule se bhi \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^{-1}) = -x^{-2}\). Dono ne ek hi jawab diya, is se formula par aitmaad barhta hai.
Ab kitab ka example dekhte hain jis mein numerator cubic (teen power wala) aur denominator quadratic hai.

blocks.title: Example 11
steps:
Given: \(\phi(x) = \frac{2x^{3} - 3x^{2} + 5}{x^{2} + 1}\).
To find: \(\phi'(x)\).
Method: \(\phi\) ek fraction (quotient) hai, is liye formula 6. Shart \(g(x) \ne 0\) check karein: \(x^{2} + 1 \ge 1\), yani denominator kabhi zero nahin hota, is liye har real \(x\) par rule chalega. Plan: \(f\), \(g\), \(f'\), \(g'\) alag alag nikaalein, phir formula mein rakhein.

Step 1: Numerator aur denominator ke naam rakhein
\[f(x) = 2x^{3} - 3x^{2} + 5\]
\[g(x) = x^{2} + 1\]
Kyun: quotient rule mein chaar cheezein chahiye; pehle unhein saaf alag likh lena ghaltiyon se bachata hai.
Dhyan dein: kitab yahan \(f(x)\) ko \(2x^{2} - 3x^{2} + 5\) chhaapti hai; sahi \(2x^{3}\) hai (neeche \"Kitab ki ghalti\").

Step 2: Numerator ka derivative
\[f'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}[2x^{3} - 3x^{2} + 5]\]
\[= 2(3x^{2}) - 3(2x) + 0 = 6x^{2} - 6x\]
Kyun: formulas 1, 3, 4 aur power rule: har term alag, constants bahar, aur 5 ka derivative zero.

Step 3: Denominator ka derivative
\[g'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}[x^{2} + 1] = 2x + 0 = 2x\]
Kyun: \(x^{2}\) ka derivative \(2x\), aur 1 constant hai.

Step 4: Quotient formula mein rakhein
\[\phi'(x) = \dfrac{f'(x)g(x) - f(x)g'(x)}{[g(x)]^{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{(6x^{2} - 6x)(x^{2} + 1) - (2x^{3} - 3x^{2} + 5)(2x)}{(x^{2} + 1)^{2}}\]
Kyun: Steps 1 se 3 ki chaaron cheezein rakhi hain. Doosre product ko bracket mein rakha kyun ke us se pehle minus hai; yeh minus poore product par lagega.

Step 5: Dono products kholein
\[(6x^{2} - 6x)(x^{2} + 1) = 6x^{4} - 6x^{3} + 6x^{2} - 6x\]
\[(2x^{3} - 3x^{2} + 5)(2x) = 4x^{4} - 6x^{3} + 10x\]
\[\phi'(x) = \dfrac{6x^{4} - 6x^{3} + 6x^{2} - 6x - (4x^{4} - 6x^{3} + 10x)}{(x^{2} + 1)^{2}}\]
Kyun: har term ko har term se multiply kiya. Denominator ko khola nahin, kyun ke \((x^{2} + 1)^{2}\) ki shakal mein woh zyada saaf hai.

Step 6: Bracket hataein aur milti julti terms jama karein
\[= \dfrac{6x^{4} - 6x^{3} + 6x^{2} - 6x - 4x^{4} + 6x^{3} - 10x}{(x^{2} + 1)^{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{2x^{4} + 6x^{2} - 16x}{(x^{2} + 1)^{2}}\]
Kyun: bracket se pehle minus ne andar ka har sign badal diya: \(+4x^{4} \to -4x^{4}\), \(-6x^{3} \to +6x^{3}\), \(+10x \to -10x\). Phir \(6x^{4} - 4x^{4} = 2x^{4}\), \(-6x^{3} + 6x^{3} = 0\), aur \(-6x - 10x = -16x\).
Dhyan dein: sab se zyada ghaltiyan isi qadam par hoti hain, jab minus sirf pehli term par laga kar baqi bhool jaate hain.

Tasdeeq:
\(x = 1\) par hamara jawab: \(\frac{2 + 6 - 16}{4} = \frac{-8}{4} = -2\). Function se seedha: \(\frac{\phi(1.001) - \phi(0.999)}{0.002} \approx -2.0000\). Dono barabar, is liye jawab sahi hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Hal mein kitab \(f(x) = 2x^{2} - 3x^{2} + 5\) chhaapti hai; sawal ka numerator \(f(x) = 2x^{3} - 3x^{2} + 5\) hai (aage ka saara kaam kitab ne \(2x^{3}\) se hi kiya hai). Teesri line ke numerator mein \(-10x\) ke baad ek faltu \")\" bhi chhapa hai. Aakhri jawab \(\frac{2x^{4} + 6x^{2} - 16x}{(x^{2} + 1)^{2}}\) sahi hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Ab ek sawal hum khud banate hain (yeh kitab ka sawal nahin): \(y = \frac{x + 1}{x - 1}\), \(x \ne 1\).
\(f = x + 1\), \(g = x - 1\), \(f' = 1\), \(g' = 1\).
\(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1\cdot(x - 1) - (x + 1)\cdot 1}{(x - 1)^{2}} = \frac{-2}{(x - 1)^{2}}\).
Kyun: numerator mein \(x - 1 - x - 1 = -2\); \(x\) cancel ho gaya.
Tasdeeq: \(y = 1 + \frac{2}{x - 1}\) bhi likh sakte hain. \(x\) barhne par \(\frac{2}{x - 1}\) chhota hota jata hai (jab \(x > 1\)), yani \(y\) ghat'ta hai, is liye derivative negative hona hi chahiye tha. Sahi!

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\frac{d}{dx}(c) = 0\) aur \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^{n}) = nx^{n-1}\) (power neeche, power ek kam).
2. Formula 3: \(\frac{d}{dx}[cf(x)] = c\frac{d}{dx}[f(x)]\): multiply hone wala constant bahar khara rehta hai.
3. Formula 4: \((f \pm g)' = f' \pm g'\): term by term, chahe jitni terms hon.
4. Formula 5 (product): \((fg)' = f'g + fg'\).
5. Formula 6 (quotient): \(\left(\frac{f}{g}\right)' = \frac{f'g - fg'}{g^{2}}\), jahan \(g(x) \ne 0\); tarteeb zaroori hai.
6. Pehle simplify karna (Examples 8, 9) aur product rule (Example 10) ek hi jawab dete hain; jo raasta chhota ho woh chuniye.
7. Roots ko pehle powers mein likhiye: \(\sqrt{x} = x^{\frac{1}{2}}\), \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} = x^{-\frac{1}{2}}\).
8. Har jawab ko kisi aasan value (jaise \(x = 1\) ya \(x = 4\)) par check karna achhi aadat hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \((fg)' = f'g'\) likhna GHALAT hai. Misal: \(\frac{d}{dx}(x\cdot x) = 2x\), jab ke \(1\cdot 1 = 1\). Bachne ka tareeqa: product rule ka jumla zabani yaad rakhiye.
2. \(\left(\frac{f}{g}\right)' = \frac{f'}{g'}\) bhi GHALAT hai. Aur numerator mein \(fg' - f'g\) likh dena jawab ka sign ulta kar deta hai.
3. Constant term ka derivative zero ki bajaye constant hi likh dena (jaise \(\frac{d}{dx}(35) = 35\)). Yaad rakhiye: jo badalta nahin, us ki tabdeeli zero.
4. Quotient rule mein doosre product se pehle wala minus sirf pehli term par lagana. Pehle product ko bracket mein band kijiye, phir kholiye.
5. Fraction powers mein ghalti: \(\frac{1}{2} - 1 = -\frac{1}{2}\) hai, \(\frac{1}{2}\) nahin; \(\frac{4}{3} - 1 = \frac{1}{3}\).
6. \(\frac{d}{dx}(x) = 1\) ki jagah \(x\) ya 0 likhna.
